Fixes #7413 
##### Summary

[WIP] Agent cloud link

- Setup main mqtt thread to connect to a broker using V5 of the MQTT protocol (TBD)

- Send alarms to topic "netdata/alarm"

- Add error checks to handle connection failures

- Add params in new section [mqtt] for
  Broker, port
  Maximum concurrent sent  / recev messages

- Dummy function to check claiming status

- Generic mqtt_send command to publish message to a base topic , sub topic
  It will end up in the form base_topic/sub_topic

- Add host/port in the connection failure error message

issue_context.title: Initiate the Agent-Cloud-Link
issue_context.body:
When the agent is in a claimed state:

* Periodic timer to check the status of the ACL.
* If the agent is claimed and the link is not operational set up the wss + MQTT transport layer.

This will require:
* Including the libmosquito library as a dependency, sync with the SRE team.
* Add a heartbeat.
* Add error-checking.
* Tuning the connection parameters (timeouts) to be added to config.

Demo against a standard broker (VerneMq?)
comments:
#### Update

- A new thread is created to check for the mqtt_state (agent_cloud link)
  - Check to see if agent is in claimed state
  - Try to establish connection to the cloud 
     - Reads parameters (hostname, port)  from a new [mqtt] section in netdata.conf
     - Setup PING every 60 seconds (default)
- Uses MQTT Protocol version 5.0
- Setup sample subscription to a topic
  - Setup of a message callback to take action on received messages
- Assumes generic function to establish base_topic communication to the cloud (TBD)
- Periodic check for connection reinit if needed
- Check for graceful shutdown of connection (Needs more work)
- Test standard connection on localhost (mosquitto broker)
- Test standard connection on VerneMQ (docker setup)



[WIP] pull requests are appreciated :)
##### Update
- The libmosquitto library could not be used to upgrade the connection to wss
- Attempted to switch and use the libpaho library
  - Was able to use mqtt over websockets
  - Was able to use mqtt over SSL
  - Was not to use mqtt over secure websockets (seems like an issue with the libpaho C library)

##### Next steps
- Close this issue, will open a new one to focus solely on investigating the wss upgrade
- Post a comment on the libpaho project page asking about an issue that's being worked on and may resolve the failure to upgrade to secure websockets
- Focus again on the libmosquitto -- post a Q on the project for assistance (if there is a way to upgrade to wss)

review_comments: I think we can skip this - the protocol just defines a payload as an application specific stream of bytes.
yes, may not be needed..  just put a note there in case we need it
Instead to remove, would not be better to comment the code?
We will most likely go with version 5 to take advantage of  new features. It can be set to be an option and select the appropriate version as needed in the future
The protocol design is still changing but my current estimate is that we will need v5 to do the authentication properly - we can talk about this in the groom.

Only to confirm, because I did not study the library libmosquitto yet, I verified that you were reporting errors in different parts of this function, but you never returned from errors, so  I understood that the library sets default values every time that you moved in front, is my conclusion correct?

Several functions will fail becaus of incorrect arguments, others when the actual connection is attempted (e.g. you never get a connection established callback for example)

For the subscribe command more error handling will be added (also it may be moved around) depending on the agent cloud link protocol
